objective: Turn the existing CUDA/PyTorch provider prototype into an evidence-bound v0.2.0 MLIR CUDA foundation: close the pinned client contract, materialize verified Kernel IR behind the neutral protocol, lower it through backend-owned MLIR pipelines, then qualify the PyTorch CUDA corpus on CPU and Vulkan.

lanes.outcome: Freeze the pinned-client CUDA surface and prove it with a checked-in real-client gate plus complete handle and profile-identity negative coverage.
acceptance: The Driver API and profile-specific internal-table matrix classifies every required entry as implemented, typed-stubbed, observed, or MetaFlux-strengthened.
A checked-in gate runs the pinned real client through import, driver enumeration, and runtime copy against a stock daemon; fake probe self-tests are not acceptance evidence.
Function lookup reuse and invalid, stale, destroyed, and cross-module handle cases pass while surface, probe, and cache identities advance together.

lanes.outcome: Encode the pinned framework-kernel profile as an ecosystem-neutral request, materialize verified Kernel IR in the compiler worker, and execute the declared corpus through the backend-owned MLIR-to-CPU pipeline.
acceptance: The versioned framework-kernel request carries no CUDA, PyTorch, MLIR, or target-specific types; the daemon/compiler worker validates it into canonical Kernel IR.
The CUDA provider performs no tensor arithmetic or result materialization, and the CPU branch lowers verified Kernel IR through MLIR and LLVM to a validated backend artifact.
A checked-in gate reaches artifact intake and eager add, then proves the declared corpus, module intake, function resolution, cache behavior, and bit-exact CPU execution through daemon submissions.

lanes.outcome: Qualify PyTorch CUDA lifecycle semantics and execute the same canonical Kernel IR corpus through independent CPU/LLVM and Vulkan/SPIR-V MLIR branches without regressing v0.1.x.
acceptance: Stream, event, allocator, multi-stream, synchronization, teardown, and daemon-loss rows pass for the pinned client.
Framework execution selects qualified CPU and Vulkan daemon routes with bit-exact differential evidence for the same corpus manifest.
The pinned baseline and frontier gap manifests plus cumulative v0.1.x regression evidence are current and release-facing.
